+## with a live preview ball - and giving materials to surfaces (double-click, the Assign button,
+## a drag into the view; in edit mode, to the selected faces: split into a surface of their own).
+## An edit applies at once to every surface of the open model that uses the material, and is
+## one undo step (a slider dragged: one step). Saved with the model - a character's materials
+## into its model.json (the "mesh_editor_own" ones: _write_material_table), your library
+## materials into data/materials.json (or your mod's merge file).
+## A library material given to the open model becomes one Material shared by every surface it's
+## given to (meta "mat_lib_id"): editing the library entry edits that Material too.
+

+const MeshIO := preload("res://scripts/editor/mesh/mesh_io.gd")
+## The settings a character's material has (the rest: a full material's).
+const CHAR_ROWS := ["color", "metal", "rough", "emit"]
+const CHAR_NOTE := "A character's material carries only its colour, metal, roughness and glow: the game merges a character\ninto one surface with one shader and reads these from its model.json by the material's name."
+const THUMB_DELAY_MS := 400
+const PREVIEW := 112
+
+var ed: Control
+var lib: MaterialLibrary
+var browser: MaterialBrowser
+var thumbs: Node
+## The material shown in the MATERIAL panel ("": none).
+var picked := ""
+var _linked := {}          # library id -> the Material it is in the open model
+var _model_sig := ""
+var _rows := {}            # setting -> its row
+var _ctl := {}             # setting -> its control
+var _tips := {}            # setting -> its tooltip (a character's note added when it is one)
+var _tex := {}             # slot -> {thumb, replace, clear}
+var _name_l: Label
+var _info_l: Label
+var _preview: TextureRect
+var _vp: SubViewport
+var _ball: MeshInstance3D
+var _pv_mat: Material       # the preview's material (a library one not in the model: a copy of its own)
+var _pv_due := false
+var _thumb_due := {}
+var _thumb_at := 0
+var _syncing := false
+var _serial := 0            # (each pick: slider drags coalesce into one undo step only within it)
+var _dialog: FileDialog
+
+
+func setup(editor: Control) -> void:
+	ed = editor
+	name = "MaterialTools"
+	thumbs = MeshThumbs.new()
+	thumbs.name = "MaterialThumbs"
+	add_child(thumbs)

+	browser = MaterialBrowser.new()

+
+
+func _build_preview() -> void:
+	_vp = SubViewport.new()

+	var env := Environment.new()

+	env.ambient_light_energy = 0.8

+	var we := WorldEnvironment.new()
+	we.environment = env
+	_vp.add_child(we)
+	var key := DirectionalLight3D.new()
+	key.rotation_degrees = Vector3(-40, 35, 0)
+	key.light_energy = 1.6
+	_vp.add_child(key)

+	rim.rotation_degrees = Vector3(-20, 200, 0)
+	rim.light_energy = 0.8
+	rim.light_color = Color(0.7, 0.8, 1.0)
+	_vp.add_child(rim)

+	cam.fov = 32.0
+	_vp.add_child(cam)
+	cam.look_at_from_position(Vector3(0, 0.25, 1.9), Vector3.ZERO, Vector3.UP)
+	_ball = MeshInstance3D.new()

+
+
+func _process(_dt: float) -> void:
+	if _pv_due:
+		_pv_due = false
+		_vp.render_target_update_mode = SubViewport.UPDATE_ONCE
+	if not _thumb_due.is_empty() and Time.get_ticks_msec() >= _thumb_at:
+		for id in _thumb_due:

+
+
+## The MATERIAL section's settings (under the editor's surface list), into `box`.
+func build_right(box: VBoxContainer) -> void:
+	var head := HBoxContainer.new()
+	head.add_theme_constant_override("separation", 6)
+	box.add_child(head)
+	_preview = TextureRect.new()
+	_preview.name = "MaterialPreviewBall"
+	_preview.custom_minimum_size = Vector2(PREVIEW, PREVIEW) * 0.75
+	_preview.expand_mode = TextureRect.EXPAND_IGNORE_SIZE
+	_preview.stretch_mode = TextureRect.STRETCH_KEEP_ASPECT_CENTERED
+	_preview.texture = _vp.get_texture()
+	_preview.mouse_filter = Control.MOUSE_FILTER_STOP
+	_preview.tooltip_text = EditorIcons.tip("Material preview", "", "The picked material on a ball, lit as the editor's view is - drawn again as you change it.")
+	head.add_child(_preview)
+	var col := VBoxContainer.new()
+	col.size_flags_horizontal = Control.SIZE_EXPAND_FILL
+	head.add_child(col)
+	_name_l = UI.label("(no material picked)", 14, NeonTheme.HEAD)
+	_name_l.clip_text = true
+	_name_l.mouse_filter = Control.MOUSE_FILTER_STOP
+	_name_l.tooltip_text = EditorIcons.tip("Material being edited", "", "The material being edited: the selected surface's, or the one picked in the Materials tab.")
+	col.add_child(_name_l)
+	_info_l = UI.label("", 13, UI.TEXT_DIM)
+	_info_l.autowrap_mode = TextServer.AUTOWRAP_WORD_SMART
+	_info_l.custom_minimum_size.x = 100
+	_info_l.mouse_filter = Control.MOUSE_FILTER_STOP
+	col.add_child(_info_l)
+	var rows := VBoxContainer.new()
+	rows.add_theme_constant_override("separation", 2)
+	box.add_child(rows)
+	var color := ColorPickerButton.new()
+	color.custom_minimum_size = Vector2(80, 24)
+	color.color_changed.connect(func(c: Color): set_value("color", [c.r, c.g, c.b, c.a]))
+	_row(rows, "color", "Colour", color, EditorIcons.tip("Albedo colour", "", "The material's base colour (with its opacity, when Transparency is on)."))
+	_tex_row(rows, "albedo", "Albedo map", "Albedo texture", "A picture over the base colour (the colour tints it).")
+	for p in [["metal", "Metallic", 1.0, "How metallic: 0 paint, stone, cloth; 1 bare metal."], ["rough", "Roughness", 1.0, "0 mirror-smooth, 1 matt."]]:
+		_row(rows, p[0], p[1], _slider(p[0], p[2]), EditorIcons.tip(p[1], "", p[3]))
+	_tex_row(rows, "rough", "Rough map", "Roughness texture", "A picture of how rough each spot is (its grey: black smooth, white matt) - times Roughness.")
+	_row(rows, "emit", "Glow", _slider("emit", 8.0), EditorIcons.tip("Glow", "", "How brightly it glows (0: not at all) - a character's in its own colour."))
+	var emc := ColorPickerButton.new()
+	emc.custom_minimum_size = Vector2(80, 24)
+	emc.edit_alpha = false
+	emc.color_changed.connect(func(c: Color): set_value("emission", [c.r, c.g, c.b]))
+	_row(rows, "emission", "Glow colour", emc, EditorIcons.tip("Glow colour", "", "The colour it glows in (with Glow above 0)."))
+	_tex_row(rows, "emission", "Glow map", "Glow texture", "A picture of where it glows, and in what colour.")
+	_tex_row(rows, "normal", "Normal map", "Normal map", "A normal map: small bumps and dents drawn into the light without changing the mesh.")
+	_row(rows, "normal", "Bumps", _slider("normal", 4.0), EditorIcons.tip("Normal map strength", "", "How deep the normal map's bumps look (1: as drawn)."))
+	var alpha := CheckBox.new()
+	alpha.text = "See-through"
+	alpha.focus_mode = Control.FOCUS_NONE
+	alpha.add_theme_font_size_override("font_size", 14)
+	alpha.toggled.connect(func(on): set_value("alpha", on))
+	_row(rows, "alpha", "Alpha", alpha, EditorIcons.tip("Transparency", "", "The colour's opacity (and the albedo texture's) makes it see-through - glass, a visor, a hologram."))
+	var uvb := HBoxContainer.new()
+	uvb.add_theme_constant_override("separation", 2)
+	for a in 2:
+		var sp := SpinBox.new()
+		sp.min_value = 0.01
+		sp.max_value = 100.0
+		sp.step = 0.01
+		sp.allow_greater = true
+		sp.custom_minimum_size.x = 60
+		sp.size_flags_horizontal = Control.SIZE_EXPAND_FILL
+		sp.tooltip_text = EditorIcons.tip("UV scale " + "UV"[a], "", "How many times the textures repeat across the surface, %s." % ["along U (across)", "along V (up)"][a])
+		sp.value_changed.connect(func(_v): _uv_changed())
+		uvb.add_child(sp)
+		_ctl["uv%d" % a] = sp
+	_row(rows, "uv", "UV scale", uvb, EditorIcons.tip("UV scale", "", "How many times the textures repeat across the surface (U, V)."))
+	var cull := OptionButton.new()
+	cull.focus_mode = Control.FOCUS_NONE
+	cull.add_theme_font_size_override("font_size", 14)
+	for t in ["Back hidden", "Front hidden", "Both sides"]:
+		cull.add_item(t)
+	cull.item_selected.connect(func(i): set_value("cull", MaterialLibrary.CULLS[i]))
+	_row(rows, "cull", "Sides", cull, EditorIcons.tip("Cull mode", "", "Which side of each face is drawn: the front only (the usual), the back only, or both (thin\nthings seen from both sides - leaves, cloth, flags)."))
+	_show()
+
+
+func _slider(key: String, mx: float) -> HSlider:
+	var s := HSlider.new()
+	s.min_value = 0.0
+	s.max_value = mx
+	s.step = 0.01
+	s.custom_minimum_size = Vector2(90, 20)
+	s.size_flags_horizontal = Control.SIZE_EXPAND_FILL
+	s.value_changed.connect(func(v): set_value(key, v))
+	return s
+
+
+func _row(rows: VBoxContainer, key: String, label: String, c: Control, tip: String) -> void:
+	var h := HBoxContainer.new()
+	h.add_theme_constant_override("separation", 4)
+	var l := UI.label(label, 14, UI.TEXT_DIM)
+	l.custom_minimum_size.x = 84
+	l.clip_text = true
+	h.add_child(l)
+	c.size_flags_horizontal = Control.SIZE_EXPAND_FILL
+	h.add_child(c)
+	rows.add_child(h)
+	_rows[key] = h
+	if not _ctl.has(key):
+		_ctl[key] = c
+	_tips[key] = tip
+	c.tooltip_text = tip
+
+
+func _tex_row(rows: VBoxContainer, slot: String, short: String, label: String, help: String) -> void:
+	var h := HBoxContainer.new()
+	h.add_theme_constant_override("separation", 4)
+	var l := UI.label(short, 14, UI.TEXT_DIM)
+	l.custom_minimum_size.x = 84
+	l.clip_text = true
+	h.add_child(l)
+	var tr := TextureRect.new()
+	tr.custom_minimum_size = Vector2(30, 30)
+	tr.expand_mode = TextureRect.EXPAND_IGNORE_SIZE
+	tr.stretch_mode = TextureRect.STRETCH_KEEP_ASPECT_CENTERED
+	tr.mouse_filter = Control.MOUSE_FILTER_STOP
+	tr.tooltip_text = EditorIcons.tip(label, "", help + "\n(none: the square stays empty)")
+	h.add_child(tr)
+	var rep := UI.button("Replace", func(): _pick_picture(slot), 13)
+	rep.focus_mode = Control.FOCUS_NONE
+	rep.tooltip_text = EditorIcons.tip("Replace " + label.to_lower(), "", help + "\nPicks a picture of yours (PNG, JPG, WebP): it's copied into the game or your mod\n(art/materials/) when the library or the model is saved.")
+	rep.visible = not OS.has_feature("web")
+	h.add_child(rep)
+	var clr := UI.button("Clear", func(): set_texture_image(slot, null), 13)
+	clr.focus_mode = Control.FOCUS_NONE
+	clr.tooltip_text = EditorIcons.tip("Clear " + label.to_lower(), "", "Takes the picture off the material.")
+	h.add_child(clr)
+	rows.add_child(h)
+	_rows["tex_" + slot] = h
+	_tex[slot] = {"thumb": tr, "replace": rep, "clear": clr}
+	_tips["tex_" + slot] = tr.tooltip_text
+
+
+# --- the open model ------------------------------------------------------------------------
+
+func _is_char() -> bool:
+	return MeshIO.is_character(str(ed.path))
+
+
+## The open model's materials as the library's "This model" group (when they changed).
+func refresh_model() -> void:
+	var mats := []
+	for p: MeshInstance3D in ed.parts():
+		for i in p.mesh.get_surface_count():
+			var m := p.get_surface_override_material(i)
+			if m == null:
+				m = p.mesh.surface_get_material(i)
+			if m and not m in mats:
+				mats.append(m)
+	var sig := str(ed.path) + "|" + ",".join(mats.map(func(m): return str(m.get_instance_id()) + m.resource_name))
+	if sig == _model_sig:
+		return
+	_model_sig = sig
+	lib.set_model(mats, _is_char())
+	for id in _linked.keys():
+		if not is_instance_valid(_linked[id]) or not _linked[id] in mats:
+			_linked.erase(id)
+	for m: Material in mats:
+		var lid := str(m.get_meta("mat_lib_id", ""))
+		if lid != "" and lib.has(lid):
+			_linked[lid] = m
+	if picked != "" and not lib.has(picked):
+		picked = ""
+		_show()
+	if browser.is_visible_in_tree():
+		browser.refill()
+
+
+## The editor opened another model: the old one's links forgotten.
+func model_changed() -> void:
+	_linked.clear()
+	_model_sig = "-"
+	refresh_model()
+
+
+## Surface `s` of part `p` selected: its material shown.
+func show_surface(p: MeshInstance3D, s: int) -> void:
+	refresh_model()
+	var m: Material = null
+	if p and s >= 0 and s < p.mesh.get_surface_count():
+		m = p.get_surface_override_material(s)
+		if m == null:
+			m = p.mesh.surface_get_material(s)
+	pick("model:%d" % m.get_instance_id() if m else "")
+
+
+## The open model's materials that are library entry `id`'s.
+func _mats_of(id: String) -> Array:
+	var out := []
+	if _linked.has(id) and is_instance_valid(_linked[id]):
+		out.append(_linked[id])
+	for mid in lib.ids("model"):
+		var m: Material = lib.entry(mid)["mat"]
+		if str(m.get_meta("mat_lib_id", "")) == id and not m in out:
+			out.append(m)
+	return out
+
+
+# --- picking and editing -------------------------------------------------------------------
+
+func pick(id: String) -> void:
+	if id != "" and not lib.has(id):
+		id = ""
+	picked = id
+	_serial += 1
+	_pv_mat = null
+	_show()
+
+
+## The settings showing in the panel now (the rows visible) - a character's: colour, metal, roughness, glow.
+func shown_settings() -> Array:
+	var out := []
+	for k in _rows:
+		if (_rows[k] as Control).visible:
+			out.append(k)
+	return out
+
+
+func _show() -> void:
+	if _name_l == null:
+		return
+	_syncing = true
+	var e := lib.entry(picked)
+	var on := not e.is_empty()
+	var editable := lib.is_editable(picked)
+	var char: bool = on and e["kind"] == "character"
+	_name_l.text = str(e["name"]) if on else "(no material picked)"
+	var info := ""
+	var tip := ""
+	if on:
+		info = "%s · %s" % [MaterialLibrary.GROUP_LABEL[e["group"]], "character" if char else "full"]
+		var slot := MaterialLibrary.slot_of(str(e["name"]))
+		if char:
+			info += " · recolour slot: " + slot if slot != "" else " · fixed colour"
+			tip = CHAR_NOTE + ("\nNamed %s, it takes the colour a character is recoloured with (%s)." % [e["name"], slot] if slot != "" else "")
+		if not e.get("users", []).is_empty():
+			tip += "\nWorn by: " + ", ".join(e["users"])
+		if not editable:
+			info += " · built in" if e["group"] != "model" else " · a shader of its own"
+			tip += "\n" + ("A built-in look: Duplicate it (the Materials tab) to make one of your own to change." if e["group"] != "model" else "Its own shader: not editable here.")
+	_info_l.text = info
+	_info_l.tooltip_text = EditorIcons.tip("About this material", "", tip.strip_edges() if tip.strip_edges() != "" else "Its group and kind.")
+	for k in _rows:
+		(_rows[k] as Control).visible = on and (not char or k in CHAR_ROWS)
+	var v := lib.values(picked)
+	var c: Array = v["color"]
+	var cp: ColorPickerButton = _ctl["color"]
+	cp.edit_alpha = not char
+	cp.color = Color(c[0], c[1], c[2], c[3] if c.size() > 3 else 1.0)
+	for k in ["metal", "rough", "emit", "normal"]:
+		(_ctl[k] as Range).set_value_no_signal(float(v[k]))
+	var ec: Array = v["emission"]
+	(_ctl["emission"] as ColorPickerButton).color = Color(ec[0], ec[1], ec[2])
+	(_ctl["alpha"] as CheckBox).set_pressed_no_signal(bool(v["alpha"]))
+	for a in 2:
+		(_ctl["uv%d" % a] as SpinBox).set_value_no_signal(float(v["uv"][a]))
+	(_ctl["cull"] as OptionButton).select(maxi(MaterialLibrary.CULLS.find(str(v["cull"])), 0))
+	for k in _ctl:
+		var ctl: Control = _ctl[k]
+		if ctl is BaseButton:
+			(ctl as BaseButton).disabled = not editable
+		elif ctl is Range:
+			(ctl as Range).editable = editable
+		var base: String = _tips.get(k, ctl.tooltip_text if not _tips.has(k) else "")
+		if _tips.has(k):
+			ctl.tooltip_text = base + ("\n" + CHAR_NOTE if char else "") + ("" if editable or not on else "\n(built in: Duplicate it to change it)")
+	var tx := lib.textures(picked)
+	for s in _tex:
+		var r: Dictionary = _tex[s]
+		(r["thumb"] as TextureRect).texture = tx.get(s)
+		(r["replace"] as Button).disabled = not editable
+		(r["clear"] as Button).disabled = not editable or not tx.has(s)
+	_syncing = false
+	_update_preview()
+
+
+func _update_preview() -> void:
+	var e := lib.entry(picked)
+	if e.is_empty():
+		_ball.material_override = null
+		_ball.visible = false
+	else:
+		_ball.visible = true
+		var m: Material = null
+		if e["group"] == "model":
+			m = e["mat"]
+		elif _linked.has(picked) and is_instance_valid(_linked[picked]):
+			m = _linked[picked]
+		else:
+			if _pv_mat == null:
+				_pv_mat = lib.make_material(picked)
+			else:
+				MaterialLibrary.apply(_pv_mat, str(e["kind"]), lib.values(picked), e["textures"])
+			m = _pv_mat
+		_ball.material_override = m
+	_pv_due = true
+
+
+func _uv_changed() -> void:
+	set_value("uv", [(_ctl["uv0"] as SpinBox).value, (_ctl["uv1"] as SpinBox).value])
+
+
+## Sets one setting of the picked material - on every surface using it; one undo step (a
+## slider dragged: one step).
+func set_value(key: String, v: Variant) -> void:
+	if _syncing or picked == "" or not lib.is_editable(picked):
+		return
+	var id := picked
+	var before := lib.values(id)
+	var after := before.duplicate(true)
+	after[key] = v
+	_apply(id, after)
+	_step("Material " + key, func(): _apply(id, before), func(): _apply(id, after), "%d|%s|%s" % [_serial, id, key])
+
+
+## One undo step (in edit mode: of the edit's own steps); `tag` the same as the last's: that
+## step's redo replaced (a slider dragged).
+func _step(nm: String, undo_it: Callable, redo_it: Callable, tag := "") -> void:
+	var editing: bool = ed.mode == "edit"
+	var stack: Array = ed._eundo if editing else ed._undo
+	if tag != "" and not stack.is_empty() and str(stack.back().get("mat_tag", "")) == tag:
+		stack.back()["redo"] = redo_it
+		ed.dirty = true
+		return
+	if editing:
+		ed._eundo.append({"name": nm, "undo": undo_it, "redo": redo_it, "mat_tag": tag})
+		ed._eredo.clear()
+		ed.dirty = true
+		ed._update_ui()
+	else:
+		ed._push(nm, undo_it, redo_it)
+		ed._undo.back()["mat_tag"] = tag
+
+
+## Material `id` given settings `vals` (`tex`: its textures too - slot -> Texture2D for a model's,
+## slot -> res path for yours; null: as they are) - and every surface using it.
+func _apply(id: String, vals: Dictionary, tex: Variant = null) -> void:
+	var e := lib.entry(id)
+	if e.is_empty():
+		return
+	var changed := [id]
+	if e["group"] == "model":
+		var m: Material = e["mat"]
+		MaterialLibrary.apply(m, str(e["kind"]), vals, tex)
+		m.set_meta("mesh_editor_own", true)
+		var lid := str(m.get_meta("mat_lib_id", ""))
+		if lid != "" and lib.entry(lid).get("group", "") == "mine":
+			lib.set_values(lid, vals)
+			changed.append(lid)
+	else:
+		lib.set_values(id, vals)
+		if tex is Dictionary:
+			lib.set_textures(id, tex)
+		for m: Material in _mats_of(id):
+			MaterialLibrary.apply(m, str(e["kind"]), vals, lib.entry(id)["textures"])
+			if _is_char():
+				m.set_meta("mesh_editor_own", true)
+			changed.append("model:%d" % m.get_instance_id())
+	for c in changed:
+		_thumb_due[c] = true
+	_thumb_at = Time.get_ticks_msec() + THUMB_DELAY_MS
+	if picked in changed:
+		_show()
+	ed.view.request()
+
+
+## A picture for texture `slot` of the picked material (null: the texture taken off) - undoable.
+func set_texture_image(slot: String, img: Image) -> void:
+	if picked == "" or not lib.is_editable(picked):
+		return
+	var id := picked
+	var e := lib.entry(id)
+	var before: Dictionary
+	var after: Dictionary
+	if e["group"] == "model":
+		before = lib.textures(id)
+		after = before.duplicate()
+		if img:
+			img.generate_mipmaps()
+			after[slot] = ImageTexture.create_from_image(img)
+		else:
+			after.erase(slot)
+	else:
+		before = (e["textures"] as Dictionary).duplicate()
+		after = before.duplicate()
+		if img:
+			var res := lib.texture_path(id, slot)
+			lib.keep_picture(res, img)
+			after[slot] = res
+		else:
+			after.erase(slot)
+	_apply(id, lib.values(id), after)
+	_step("Material texture", func(): _apply(id, lib.values(id), before), func(): _apply(id, lib.values(id), after))
+
+
+func _pick_picture(slot: String) -> void:
+	if _dialog:
+		_dialog.queue_free()
+	_dialog = FileDialog.new()
+	_dialog.file_mode = FileDialog.FILE_MODE_OPEN_FILE
+	_dialog.access = FileDialog.ACCESS_FILESYSTEM
+	_dialog.filters = PackedStringArray(["*.png, *.jpg, *.jpeg, *.webp ; Pictures"])
+	_dialog.use_native_dialog = true
+	add_child(_dialog)
+	_dialog.file_selected.connect(func(path: String):
+		var img := Image.load_from_file(path)
+		if img == null:
+			ed._say("Couldn't read " + path.get_file())
+			return
+		set_texture_image(slot, img))
+	_dialog.popup_centered(Vector2i(900, 600))
+
+
+# --- giving materials to surfaces ----------------------------------------------------------
+
+## The Material library entry `id` is in the open model (made once, shared by every surface
+## it's given to; a character's own material of that name, if it has one).
+func material_for(id: String) -> Material:
+	var e := lib.entry(id)
+	if e.is_empty():
+		return null
+	if e["group"] == "model":
+		return e["mat"]
+	if _linked.has(id) and is_instance_valid(_linked[id]):
+		return _linked[id]
+	if _is_char():
+		for mid in lib.ids("model"):
+			var own: Material = lib.entry(mid)["mat"]
+			if own.resource_name == str(e["name"]):
+				return own
+	var m := lib.make_material(id)
+	if _is_char():
+		m.set_meta("mesh_editor_own", true)   # (written into its model.json when saved)
+	_linked[id] = m
+	return m
+
+
+## Gives material `id` to surface `s` of part `p` (undoable).
+func assign(id: String, p: MeshInstance3D, s: int) -> void:
+	var m := material_for(id)
+	if m == null or p == null:
+		return
+	ed.set_surface_material(p, s, m)
+	refresh_model()
+	ed._say("%s given to %s's surface %d." % [lib.entry(id)["name"], p.name, s + 1])
+
+
+## Gives material `id` (""): the browser's pick, else the panel's) to the selected faces (edit
+## mode), else to the selected part's surface.
+func assign_selected(id := "") -> void:
+	if id == "":
+		id = browser.selected() if browser.selected() != "" else picked
+	if id == "" or not lib.has(id):
+		ed._say("Pick a material in the Materials tab first.")
+		return
+	if ed.mode == "edit" and ed.em and ed.sel_t.has(1):
+		assign_faces(id)
+		return
+	if ed.part == null:
+		ed._say("Select a part first: the material goes to its surface (the MATERIAL panel's Surface).")
+		return
+	assign(id, ed.part, maxi(ed._surface_index(), 0))
+
+
+## Edit mode: material `id` given to the selected faces - split into a surface of their own if
+## they're only some of theirs (one edit step).
+func assign_faces(id: String) -> void:
+	var em = ed.em
+	if em == null:
+		return
+	var ts: PackedByteArray = em.grow_to_polys(ed.sel_t.duplicate())
+	if not ts.has(1):
+		ed._say("Select faces first.")
+		return
+	var m := material_for(id)
+	var before: Dictionary = ed._snap()
+	var now: PackedByteArray = em.split_to_surface(ts, m)
+	ed._resize_sel()
+	ed.select_all(false)
+	for t in mini(now.size(), ed.sel_t.size()):
+		ed.sel_t[t] = now[t]
+	ed._derive_sel()
+	ed._edit_done("Material", before)
+	ed._show_material_list()
+	refresh_model()
+	var n := _count(now)
+	ed._say("%s given to the selected faces (%d triangle%s)." % [lib.entry(id)["name"], n, "" if n == 1 else "s"])
+
+
+static func _count(sel: PackedByteArray) -> int:
+	var n := 0
+	for b in sel:
+		n += b
+	return n
+
+
+## The part, surface and triangle under `at` in the view ([] - none).
+func surface_at(at: Vector2) -> Array:
+	var r: Array = ed.view.ray(at)
+	var best := INF
+	var out := []
+	for p: MeshInstance3D in ed.parts():
+		if not p.is_visible_in_tree():
+			continue
+		var tm := p.mesh.generate_triangle_mesh()
+		if tm == null:
+			continue
+		var inv := p.global_transform.affine_inverse()
+		var h := tm.intersect_ray(inv * (r[0] as Vector3), (inv.basis * (r[1] as Vector3)).normalized())
+		if h.is_empty():
+			continue
+		var d: float = (p.global_transform * (h["position"] as Vector3)).distance_to(r[0])
+		if d < best:
+			best = d
+			out = [p, _surface_of(p.mesh, int(h.get("face_index", 0))), int(h.get("face_index", 0))]
+	return out
+
+
+## The surface triangle `fi` of the mesh's faces (as Mesh.get_faces() lists them) is in.
+static func _surface_of(m: Mesh, fi: int) -> int:
+	for s in m.get_surface_count():
+		if m.surface_get_primitive_type(s) != Mesh.PRIMITIVE_TRIANGLES:
+			continue
+		var n := 0
+		if m is ArrayMesh:
+			var am := m as ArrayMesh
+			n = am.surface_get_array_index_len(s)
+			if n <= 0:
+				n = am.surface_get_array_len(s)
+		else:
+			var a := m.surface_get_arrays(s)
+			n = (a[Mesh.ARRAY_INDEX] as PackedInt32Array).size() if a[Mesh.ARRAY_INDEX] != null else (a[Mesh.ARRAY_VERTEX] as PackedVector3Array).size()
+		n /= 3
+		if fi < n:
+			return s
+		fi -= n
+	return maxi(m.get_surface_count() - 1, 0)
+
+
+func can_drop(data: Variant) -> bool:
+	return data is Dictionary and data.has("mesh_material") and lib.has(str(data["mesh_material"]))
+
+
+## A material dropped on the view: given to the surface under it (in edit mode, onto a selected
+## face: to the selected faces).
+func drop(at: Vector2, data: Variant) -> void:
+	var id := str(data["mesh_material"])
+	var hit := surface_at(at)
+	if hit.is_empty():
+		ed._say("Drop a material on a surface of the model.")
+		return
+	var p: MeshInstance3D = hit[0]
+	if ed.mode == "edit" and p == ed.part and int(hit[2]) < ed.sel_t.size() and ed.sel_t[int(hit[2])]:
+		assign_faces(id)
+		return
+	if ed.mode != "edit" and p != ed.part:
+		ed.select_part(p)
+	assign(id, p, int(hit[1]))
+
+
+# --- the library's buttons -----------------------------------------------------------------
+
+func _action(what: String) -> void:
+	match what:
+		"new": new_material()
+		"duplicate": duplicate_material()
+		"rename": rename_dialog()
+		"delete": delete_material()
+
+
+func _sel() -> String:
+	return browser.selected() if browser.selected() != "" else picked
+
+
+func _added(id: String) -> void:
+	save_library()
+	if browser.group != "" and browser.group != "mine":
+		browser.set_group("mine")
+	else:
+		browser.refill()
+	browser.select_id(id)
+	pick(id)
+
+
+## A new material of yours (a character's kind when a character is open); its id.
+func new_material() -> String:
+	var id := lib.add("New material", "character" if _is_char() else "standard", MaterialLibrary.defaults())
+	_added(id)
+	ed._say("A new material (Mine): change it in the MATERIAL panel, then double-click it or drag it onto a surface.")
+	return id
+
+
+## A copy of the picked material as yours; its id.
+func duplicate_material() -> String:
+	var src := _sel()
+	if src == "":
+		ed._say("Pick a material to duplicate.")
+		return ""
+	var id := lib.duplicate_entry(src)
+	_added(id)
+	ed._say("Duplicated as %s (Mine)." % lib.entry(id)["name"])
+	return id
+
+
+func rename_dialog() -> void:
+	var id := _sel()
+	if id == "":
+		return
+	if lib.entry(id)["group"] != "mine":
+		ed._say("Only your own materials can be renamed (a character's are found by their names; duplicate a built-in look to name your own).")
+		return
+	var layer := CanvasLayer.new()
+	layer.layer = 50
+	layer.name = "MaterialDialog"
+	ed.add_child(layer)
+	var root := Control.new()
+	root.set_anchors_preset(Control.PRESET_FULL_RECT)
+	layer.add_child(root)
+	var box := UI.modal(root, Color(1.0, 0.72, 0.38), Vector2(520, 0))
+	box.add_child(UI.label("Rename material", 24, NeonTheme.HEAD))
+	var le := LineEdit.new()
+	le.text = str(lib.entry(id)["name"])
+	le.custom_minimum_size.x = 360
+	le.add_theme_font_size_override("font_size", 16)
+	le.tooltip_text = EditorIcons.tip("Material name", "Enter", "Its new name (a character's table keeps a material by its name).")
+	box.add_child(le)
+	var row := HBoxContainer.new()
+	row.alignment = BoxContainer.ALIGNMENT_END
+	row.add_theme_constant_override("separation", 12)
+	box.add_child(row)
+	var ok := func():
+		var n := le.text.strip_edges()
+		if n == "":
+			return
+		layer.queue_free()
+		rename_material(id, n)
+	le.text_submitted.connect(func(_t): ok.call())
+	var cancel := UI.button("Cancel", layer.queue_free, 16)
+	cancel.tooltip_text = EditorIcons.tip("Cancel", "Esc", "Keeps its name.")
+	row.add_child(cancel)
+	var keep := UI.button("Rename", ok, 16)
+	keep.tooltip_text = EditorIcons.tip("Rename", "Enter", "Gives it the new name.")
+	row.add_child(keep)
+	le.grab_focus.call_deferred()
+
+
+func rename_material(id: String, n: String) -> void:
+	lib.rename(id, n)
+	for m: Material in _mats_of(id):
+		m.resource_name = n
+	save_library()
+	browser.refill()
+	browser.select_id(id)
+	_show()
+
+
+## Removes the picked material from the library (yours; a built-in look only in a mod, asked first).
+func delete_material(confirmed := false) -> void:
+	var id := _sel()
+	if id == "":
+		return
+	var e := lib.entry(id)
+	if e["group"] == "model":
+		ed._say("A material of the model itself: give its surfaces another material instead.")
+		return
+	if lib.is_builtin(id):
+		if not EditTarget.is_mod():
+			ed._say("The game's own looks can be removed only in a mod (Mods > Mod Editor): duplicate one to make your own.")
+			return
+		if not confirmed:
+			UI.confirm(ed, "Remove a built-in look?", "%s is one of the game's looks. Remove it from the material library in your mod?" % e["name"],
+				func(): delete_material(true), "Remove", "Cancel")
+			return
+	lib.remove(id)
+	_linked.erase(id)
+	save_library()
+	if picked == id:
+		pick("")
+	browser.refill()
+	ed._say("Removed the material %s from the library (surfaces that have it keep it)." % e["name"])
+
+
+## Writes the library (your materials, the pictures picked) if it changed. OK or an error.
+func save_library() -> int:
+	if not lib.dirty and lib.pending.is_empty():
+		return OK
+	var err := lib.save()
+	if err != OK:
+		ed._say("Couldn't save the material library (%s)." % error_string(err))
+	return err

files.explanation: Parts bound to a character's skeleton: each vertex weighted to its nearest bones (up to 4, inverse distance squared to each bone segment) or all to one; moved into bind space so it's drawn where it was.

hunks.diff:
@@ -1,0 +1,212 @@ 
+extends RefCounted
+## Parts bound to a character's skeleton (the mesh editor's Bind): a part added beside a
+## skinned Body is skinned to the same skeleton - each vertex weighted to its nearest
+## bones (up to four, by inverse distance squared to each bone's segment, normalised), or
+## all to one bone - so it moves with the character's animations. Its vertices are put
+## where its skin draws them as they are on screen now: in the character's T-pose (the
+## part then carries the Body's T-pose metas, and is turned back with it when saved) or
+## in the pose the skeleton has.
+
+const TPose := preload("res://scripts/editor/mesh/tpose.gd")
+const MAX_BONES := 4
+
+
+## The model's rig: the skinned part (named Body if there is one) among `parts` - {"body",
+## "skel", "skin", "tpose": T-posed, "g": each bone's global pose (the skeleton's space,
+## as drawn now), "mats": each skin bind's matrix (pose * bind)} - or {} (none).
+static func rig_of(parts: Array) -> Dictionary:
+	var body: MeshInstance3D = null
+	for p: MeshInstance3D in parts:
+		var skinned := p.has_meta("tpose") or (p.skin != null and TPose.skeleton_of(p) != null)
+		if skinned and not p.has_meta("bound_part") and (body == null or str(p.name) == "Body"):
+			body = p
+	if body == null:
+		return {}
+	var tp := body.has_meta("tpose")
+	var skel: Skeleton3D = body.get_node_or_null(body.get_meta("tpose_skel")) as Skeleton3D if tp else TPose.skeleton_of(body)
+	var skin: Skin = body.get_meta("tpose_skin") if tp else body.skin
+	if skel == null or skin == null:
+		return {}
+	var g: Array
+	var mats: Array
+	if tp:
+		g = TPose.pose(skel)
+		mats = body.get_meta("tpose_mats")
+	else:
+		g = []
+		for i in skel.get_bone_count():
+			g.append(skel.get_bone_global_pose(i))
+		mats = TPose.matrices(body, skel, g)
+	return {"body": body, "skel": skel, "skin": skin, "tpose": tp, "g": g, "mats": mats}
+
+
+## Each skin bind's bone (-1: none) and its name.
+static func binds(rig: Dictionary) -> Array:
+	var skin: Skin = rig["skin"]
+	var skel: Skeleton3D = rig["skel"]
+	var out := []
+	for k in skin.get_bind_count():
+		var b := skin.get_bind_bone(k)
+		if b < 0:
+			b = skel.find_bone(skin.get_bind_name(k))
+		out.append([b, skel.get_bone_name(b) if b >= 0 else str(skin.get_bind_name(k))])
+	return out
+
+
+## Each bind's bone as a segment (skeleton space): [from, to] - to its first child, or (a
+## bone at the end) along its own axis.
+static func _segments(rig: Dictionary) -> Array:
+	var skel: Skeleton3D = rig["skel"]
+	var g: Array = rig["g"]
+	var out := []
+	for bk in binds(rig):
+		var b: int = bk[0]
+		if b < 0:
+			out.append([])
+			continue
+		var a: Vector3 = (g[b] as Transform3D).origin
+		var e := a
+		var kids := skel.get_bone_children(b)
+		if not kids.is_empty():
+			e = (g[kids[0]] as Transform3D).origin
+		if e.distance_to(a) < 1e-4:
+			var p := skel.get_bone_parent(b)
+			var l := 0.08 if p < 0 else maxf(0.04, (g[p] as Transform3D).origin.distance_to(a) * 0.5)
+			e = a + (g[b] as Transform3D).basis.y.normalized() * l
+		out.append([a, e])
+	return out
+
+
+## The bind matrix blend of bones `bs` weights `ws`.
+static func _blend(mats: Array, bs: PackedInt32Array, ws: PackedFloat32Array) -> Transform3D:
+	var basis := Basis(Vector3.ZERO, Vector3.ZERO, Vector3.ZERO)
+	var origin := Vector3.ZERO
+	for i in bs.size():
+		var t: Transform3D = mats[bs[i]]
+		basis.x += t.basis.x * ws[i]
+		basis.y += t.basis.y * ws[i]
+		basis.z += t.basis.z * ws[i]
+		origin += t.origin * ws[i]
+	return Transform3D(basis, origin)
+
+
+## Part `p`'s mesh bound to `rig`: each vertex's bones and weights (to its nearest bones, or
+## all to skin bind `bind` when >= 0), and its place in the Body's mesh space - where its
+## skin draws it now is where it is on screen. Returns the new mesh (the part is then to
+## take the Body's global transform, skin and skeleton - or, T-posed, its T-pose metas).
+static func bound_mesh(p: MeshInstance3D, rig: Dictionary, bind := -1) -> ArrayMesh:
+	var body: MeshInstance3D = rig["body"]
+	var skel: Skeleton3D = rig["skel"]
+	var mats: Array = rig["mats"]
+	var to_skel := skel.global_transform.affine_inverse() * p.global_transform
+	var to_body := body.global_transform.affine_inverse() * p.global_transform
+	var segs := _segments(rig)
+	var names := binds(rig)
+	var src: Mesh = p.mesh
+	var out := ArrayMesh.new()
+	for si in src.get_surface_count():
+		var a := src.surface_get_arrays(si)
+		var vs: PackedVector3Array = a[Mesh.ARRAY_VERTEX]
+		var ns: PackedVector3Array = a[Mesh.ARRAY_NORMAL] if a[Mesh.ARRAY_NORMAL] != null else PackedVector3Array()
+		var bones := PackedInt32Array()
+		var weights := PackedFloat32Array()
+		for i in vs.size():
+			var q: Vector3 = to_skel * vs[i]
+			var bs := PackedInt32Array()
+			var ws := PackedFloat32Array()
+			if bind >= 0:
+				bs.append(bind)
+				ws.append(1.0)
+			else:
+				var near := []   # [distance, bind]
+				for k in segs.size():
+					var sg: Array = segs[k]
+					if sg.is_empty() or str(names[k][1]).to_lower() in TPose.WEAPON_BONES:
+						continue
+					var d := q.distance_to(Geometry3D.get_closest_point_to_segment(q, sg[0], sg[1]))
+					near.append([d, k])
+				near.sort_custom(func(x, y): return x[0] < y[0])
+				var total := 0.0
+				for j in mini(MAX_BONES, near.size()):
+					if j > 0 and near[j][0] > near[0][0] * 2.5 + 0.02:
+						break   # (only bones about as near as the nearest)
+					var w := 1.0 / pow(maxf(near[j][0], 0.005), 2.0)
+					bs.append(near[j][1])
+					ws.append(w)
+					total += w
+				for j in ws.size():
+					ws[j] /= total
+			for j in MAX_BONES:
+				bones.append(bs[j] if j < bs.size() else 0)
+				weights.append(ws[j] if j < ws.size() else 0.0)
+			if rig["tpose"]:
+				vs[i] = to_body * vs[i]
+				if i < ns.size():
+					ns[i] = (to_body.basis * ns[i]).normalized()
+			else:
+				var m := _blend(mats, bs, ws)
+				vs[i] = m.affine_inverse() * q
+				if i < ns.size():
+					ns[i] = (m.basis.inverse() * (to_skel.basis * ns[i])).normalized()
+		a[Mesh.ARRAY_VERTEX] = vs
+		if not ns.is_empty():
+			a[Mesh.ARRAY_NORMAL] = ns
+		a[Mesh.ARRAY_TANGENT] = null
+		a[Mesh.ARRAY_BONES] = bones
+		a[Mesh.ARRAY_WEIGHTS] = weights
+		out.add_surface_from_arrays(src.surface_get_primitive_type(si), a)
+		out.surface_set_material(out.get_surface_count() - 1, src.surface_get_material(si))
+		out.surface_set_name(out.get_surface_count() - 1, src.surface_get_name(si) if src is ArrayMesh else "")
+	return out
+
+
+## A bound part's mesh let go of its bones: its vertices where they're drawn now (in the
+## Body's space, the part to keep the Body's global transform), no weights.
+static func unbound_mesh(p: MeshInstance3D, rig: Dictionary) -> ArrayMesh:
+	var src: Mesh = p.mesh
+	var skel: Skeleton3D = rig["skel"]
+	var body: MeshInstance3D = rig["body"]
+	var mats: Array = rig["mats"]
+	var skel_to_body := body.global_transform.affine_inverse() * skel.global_transform
+	var out := ArrayMesh.new()
+	for si in src.get_surface_count():
+		var a := src.surface_get_arrays(si)
+		var vs: PackedVector3Array = a[Mesh.ARRAY_VERTEX]
+		var ns: PackedVector3Array = a[Mesh.ARRAY_NORMAL] if a[Mesh.ARRAY_NORMAL] != null else PackedVector3Array()
+		var bones: PackedInt32Array = a[Mesh.ARRAY_BONES] if a[Mesh.ARRAY_BONES] != null else PackedInt32Array()
+		var weights: PackedFloat32Array = a[Mesh.ARRAY_WEIGHTS] if a[Mesh.ARRAY_WEIGHTS] != null else PackedFloat32Array()
+		var per := bones.size() / vs.size() if vs.size() > 0 else 0
+		if not rig["tpose"] and per > 0:
+			for i in vs.size():
+				var m := _blend(mats, bones.slice(i * per, i * per + per), weights.slice(i * per, i * per + per))
+				vs[i] = skel_to_body * (m * vs[i])
+				if i < ns.size():
+					ns[i] = (skel_to_body.basis * (m.basis * ns[i])).normalized()
+		a[Mesh.ARRAY_VERTEX] = vs
+		if not ns.is_empty():
+			a[Mesh.ARRAY_NORMAL] = ns
+		a[Mesh.ARRAY_BONES] = null
+		a[Mesh.ARRAY_WEIGHTS] = null
+		a[Mesh.ARRAY_TANGENT] = null
+		out.add_surface_from_arrays(src.surface_get_primitive_type(si), a)
+		out.surface_set_material(out.get_surface_count() - 1, src.surface_get_material(si))
+		out.surface_set_name(out.get_surface_count() - 1, src.surface_get_name(si) if src is ArrayMesh else "")
+	return out
+
+
+## The skin bind nearest point `at` (global) - for "Bind to bone" with none picked.
+static func nearest_bind(rig: Dictionary, at: Vector3) -> int:
+	var skel: Skeleton3D = rig["skel"]
+	var q := skel.global_transform.affine_inverse() * at
+	var best := -1
+	var bd := INF
+	var segs := _segments(rig)
+	for k in segs.size():
+		var sg: Array = segs[k]
+		if sg.is_empty():
+			continue
+		var d := q.distance_to(Geometry3D.get_closest_point_to_segment(q, sg[0], sg[1]))
+		if d < bd:
+			bd = d
+			best = k
+	return best

files.explanation: Booleans of two parts by Godot's CSG on a worker: union, difference, intersection, slice; open meshes refused with the reason.

hunks.diff:
@@ -1,0 +1,125 @@ 
+extends RefCounted
+## The mesh editor's boolean operations between two parts - union, difference
+## (A minus B), intersection, and slice (A cut by B into two parts: what's inside
+## B and what's outside) - by Godot's CSG (its manifold-based solver): the two
+## meshes as CSGMesh3Ds under a CSGCombiner3D, baked into one mesh. The nodes
+## never enter the scene tree, so it runs on a worker thread (roots made ready
+## a frame ahead: prepare() / take()). Each surface keeps
+## its material (the faces B cuts into A carry B's materials). Both meshes must be
+## closed (every edge shared by two faces): an open one is refused, with the reason.
+##   MeshBool.run(a_mesh, b_mesh, b_in_a, "difference") -> {meshes: [ArrayMesh], error: ""}
+
+const Shapes := preload("res://scripts/editor/mesh/shapes.gd")
+const OPS := ["union", "difference", "intersection", "slice"]
+const LABEL := {"union": "Union", "difference": "Difference", "intersection": "Intersection", "slice": "Slice"}
+
+
+## Why `mesh` can't take part in a boolean ("" - it can).
+static func problem(mesh: Mesh, who := "the part") -> String:
+	if mesh == null or mesh.get_surface_count() == 0:
+		return "%s has no mesh" % who
+	for s in mesh.get_surface_count():
+		if mesh.surface_get_primitive_type(s) != Mesh.PRIMITIVE_TRIANGLES:
+			return "%s isn't made of triangles" % who
+	var open := Shapes.open_edges(mesh, 1e-5)
+	if open > 0:
+		return "%s isn't closed (%d open edge%s - a hole in its skin, or a flat sheet): a boolean needs a solid" % [who, open, "" if open == 1 else "s"]
+	return ""
+
+
+## Roots for run() on a worker - made here, on the main thread, a frame ahead (`n`: one for
+## each pass - slice needs 2). A CSG root queues a deferred rebuild on the main thread the
+## first time it's changed; were that queued from the worker, the main thread would rebuild
+## it while the worker does - a crash. So each root is changed here first (queued, dirty),
+## parented hidden under a holder (so the queued rebuild finds it isn't a root and does
+## nothing - and the holder's own rebuild skips it, a hidden child: it stays dirty); then
+## take() a frame later frees the holders: dirty roots that queue nothing more.
+static func prepare(n: int) -> Array:
+	var out := []
+	for i in n:
+		var holder := CSGCombiner3D.new()
+		var r := CSGCombiner3D.new()
+		r.operation = CSGShape3D.OPERATION_INTERSECTION
+		r.operation = CSGShape3D.OPERATION_UNION
+		r.visible = false
+		holder.add_child(r)
+		out.append([holder, r])
+	return out
+
+
+## The roots prepare() made (call it a frame later - after the queued calls ran), the holders freed.
+static func take(prepared: Array) -> Array:
+	var roots := []
+	for hr in prepared:
+		var holder: Node = hr[0]
+		holder.remove_child(hr[1])
+		holder.free()
+		roots.append(hr[1])
+	return roots
+
+
+## The boolean `op` of mesh `a` and mesh `b` (placed by `b_in_a` in a's space): the
+## result's meshes in a's space (slice: [inside B, outside B]) - or an error. On a worker:
+## pass `roots` (prepare() / take()); without them it runs on the main thread.
+static func run(a: Mesh, b: Mesh, b_in_a: Transform3D, op: String, roots := []) -> Dictionary:
+	var why := problem(a, "A")
+	if why == "":
+		why = problem(b, "B")
+	if why == "" and not op in OPS:
+		why = "no such operation: " + op
+	if why != "":
+		for r in roots:
+			(r as Node).free()
+		return {"meshes": [], "error": why}
+	var outs := []
+	var ops: Array = [op] if op != "slice" else ["intersection", "difference"]
+	var err := ""
+	for k in ops.size():
+		var o: String = ops[k]
+		var m := _bake(a, b, b_in_a, o, roots[k] if k < roots.size() else null)
+		if err != "":
+			continue
+		if m == null or m.get_surface_count() == 0:
+			if op == "slice":
+				err = "B doesn't cut A in two (nothing %s B)" % ("inside" if o == "intersection" else "outside")
+			else:
+				err = "nothing is left (the parts don't overlap)" if o == "intersection" else "nothing is left"
+			continue
+		outs.append(m)
+	for k in range(ops.size(), roots.size()):
+		(roots[k] as Node).free()
+	if err != "":
+		return {"meshes": [], "error": err}
+	return {"meshes": outs, "error": ""}
+
+
+static func _bake(a: Mesh, b: Mesh, b_in_a: Transform3D, op: String, root: CSGCombiner3D = null) -> ArrayMesh:
+	if root == null:
+		root = CSGCombiner3D.new()
+	# (children parented before they're changed: their changes go to the root - dirty already)
+	var ca := CSGMesh3D.new()
+	root.add_child(ca)
+	ca.mesh = a
+	var cb := CSGMesh3D.new()
+	root.add_child(cb)
+	cb.operation = {"union": CSGShape3D.OPERATION_UNION, "difference": CSGShape3D.OPERATION_SUBTRACTION,
+		"intersection": CSGShape3D.OPERATION_INTERSECTION}[op]
+	cb.transform = b_in_a
+	cb.mesh = b
+	root.call("_update_shape")   # (out of the tree: built now, not deferred)
+	var baked := root.bake_static_mesh()
+	root.free()
+	if baked == null:
+		return null
+	# each surface indexed (shared corners welded) - lighter, and edit mode welds less
+	var out := ArrayMesh.new()
+	for s in baked.get_surface_count():
+		var arr := baked.surface_get_arrays(s)
+		if (arr[Mesh.ARRAY_VERTEX] as PackedVector3Array).is_empty():
+			continue
+		var st := SurfaceTool.new()
+		st.create_from_arrays(arr)
+		st.index()
+		out.add_surface_from_arrays(Mesh.PRIMITIVE_TRIANGLES, st.commit_to_arrays())
+		out.surface_set_material(out.get_surface_count() - 1, baked.surface_get_material(s))
+	return out if out.get_surface_count() > 0 else null

@@ -1,0 +1,274 @@ 
+extends RefCounted
+## The mesh editor's files: finding the models (the game's and the mod's),
+## reading them (glTF / glb, OBJ, a mesh resource), writing glb, and the
+## primitives a new part starts from. Static; reading runs on worker threads
+## (nothing here touches the scene tree).
+
+const EXTS := ["glb", "gltf", "obj", "tres", "res"]
+const SKIP := ["res://.godot", "res://external", "res://addons", "res://builds", "res://export", "res://.git", "res://art/overrides"]
+const PRIMITIVES := ["box", "cylinder", "cone", "sphere", "plane", "torus"]
+
+
+## Every model under res:// (and the mod's own files when `mod_root` isn't ""):
+## res:// paths, the game's characters (art/*_3d/) first.
+static func scan(mod_root := "") -> PackedStringArray:
+	var found := {}
+	_walk("res://", found)
+	if mod_root != "":
+		var mod := {}
+		_walk(mod_root, mod)
+		for p in mod:
+			found["res://" + str(p).trim_prefix(mod_root)] = true
+	var out := PackedStringArray(found.keys())
+	out.sort()
+	var chars := PackedStringArray()
+	var rest := PackedStringArray()
+	for p in out:
+		(chars if is_character(p) else rest).append(p)
+	chars.append_array(rest)
+	return chars
+
+
+static func _walk(dir: String, out: Dictionary) -> void:
+	if dir.trim_suffix("/") in SKIP:
+		return
+	var d := DirAccess.open(dir)
+	if d == null:
+		return
+	d.include_hidden = false
+	for f in d.get_files():
+		var name := f.trim_suffix(".remap").trim_suffix(".import")
+		if name != f and f.ends_with(".import") and FileAccess.file_exists(dir.path_join(name)):
+			continue   # (the file itself is listed)
+		var ext := name.get_extension().to_lower()
+		if not ext in EXTS:
+			continue
+		var p := dir.path_join(name)
+		if ext == "tres" and not _is_mesh_tres(dir.path_join(f)):
+			continue
+		if ext == "res" and not name.to_lower().contains("mesh"):
+			continue
+		out[p] = true
+	for sub in d.get_directories():
+		if not sub.begins_with("."):
+			_walk(dir.path_join(sub), out)
+
+
+static func _is_mesh_tres(path: String) -> bool:
+	var f := FileAccess.open(path, FileAccess.READ)
+	if f == null:
+		return false
+	var head := f.get_line()
+	return head.contains("Mesh\"") and not head.contains("MeshLibrary")
+
+
+## One of the Blender-made characters (art/<id>_3d/), rebuilt by the pipeline.
+static func is_character(path: String) -> bool:
+	return path.begins_with("res://art/") and path.get_base_dir().ends_with("_3d")
+
+
+## Reads the model at `file` (an actual file: res:// or the mod's) - a root
+## Node3D with its parts, skeleton and animations. Null if it can't.
+static func read(file: String) -> Node3D:
+	var ext := file.get_extension().to_lower()
+	match ext:
+		"glb", "gltf":
+			if FileAccess.file_exists(file):
+				var doc := GLTFDocument.new()
+				var st := GLTFState.new()
+				if doc.append_from_file(file, st) == OK:
+					var n := doc.generate_scene(st)
+					if n is Node3D:
+						n.name = file.get_file().get_basename()
+						return n
+					if n:
+						n.free()
+			if file.begins_with("res://") and ResourceLoader.exists(file):   # (an exported game: the imported scene)
+				var ps = ResourceLoader.load(file)
+				if ps is PackedScene:
+					var n: Node = ps.instantiate()
+					if n is Node3D:
+						return n
+					n.free()
+		"obj":
+			var m: Mesh = obj_mesh(file) if FileAccess.file_exists(file) else null
+			if m == null and file.begins_with("res://") and ResourceLoader.exists(file):
+				m = ResourceLoader.load(file) as Mesh
+			if m:
+				return _wrap(m, file)
+		"tres", "res":
+			var r = ResourceLoader.load(file, "", ResourceLoader.CACHE_MODE_IGNORE)
+			if r is Mesh:
+				return _wrap(r.duplicate(true), file)
+	return null
+
+
+static func _wrap(m: Mesh, file: String) -> Node3D:
+	var root := Node3D.new()
+	root.name = file.get_file().get_basename()
+	var mi := MeshInstance3D.new()
+	mi.name = "Mesh"
+	mi.mesh = m
+	root.add_child(mi)
+	mi.owner = root
+	return root
+
+
+## A Wavefront OBJ (v / vt / vn / f, polygons as fans; materials by `usemtl`
+## become surfaces).
+static func obj_mesh(file: String) -> ArrayMesh:
+	var text := FileAccess.get_file_as_string(file)
+	if text == "":
+		return null
+	var v := PackedVector3Array()
+	var vt := PackedVector2Array()
+	var vn := PackedVector3Array()
+	var groups := {}   # material name -> SurfaceTool
+	var order := []
+	var st: SurfaceTool = null
+	var cur := ""
+	for line in text.split("\n"):
+		var w := line.strip_edges().split(" ", false)
+		if w.is_empty():
+			continue
+		match w[0]:
+			"v":
+				if w.size() >= 4:
+					v.append(Vector3(w[1].to_float(), w[2].to_float(), w[3].to_float()))
+			"vt":
+				if w.size() >= 3:
+					vt.append(Vector2(w[1].to_float(), 1.0 - w[2].to_float()))
+			"vn":
+				if w.size() >= 4:
+					vn.append(Vector3(w[1].to_float(), w[2].to_float(), w[3].to_float()))
+			"usemtl":
+				cur = w[1] if w.size() > 1 else ""
+				st = null
+			"f":
+				if st == null:
+					if not groups.has(cur):
+						var s := SurfaceTool.new()
+						s.begin(Mesh.PRIMITIVE_TRIANGLES)
+						groups[cur] = s
+						order.append(cur)
+					st = groups[cur]
+				var corners := []
+				for k in range(1, w.size()):
+					var ix := w[k].split("/")
+					var c := [_obj_i(ix[0], v.size()), -1, -1]
+					if ix.size() > 1 and ix[1] != "":
+						c[1] = _obj_i(ix[1], vt.size())
+					if ix.size() > 2 and ix[2] != "":
+						c[2] = _obj_i(ix[2], vn.size())
+					corners.append(c)
+				for k in range(1, corners.size() - 1):
+					for c in [corners[0], corners[k + 1], corners[k]]:   # (OBJ is counter-clockwise; Godot's front faces are clockwise)
+						if c[2] >= 0 and c[2] < vn.size():
+							st.set_normal(vn[c[2]])
+						if c[1] >= 0 and c[1] < vt.size():
+							st.set_uv(vt[c[1]])
+						if c[0] >= 0 and c[0] < v.size():
+							st.add_vertex(v[c[0]])
+	var mesh := ArrayMesh.new()
+	for g in order:
+		var s: SurfaceTool = groups[g]
+		if vn.is_empty():
+			s.generate_normals()
+		s.index()
+		s.commit(mesh)
+		mesh.surface_set_name(mesh.get_surface_count() - 1, g)
+	return mesh if mesh.get_surface_count() > 0 else null
+
+
+static func _obj_i(s: String, n: int) -> int:
+	var i := s.to_int()
+	return i - 1 if i > 0 else n + i
+
+
+## Writes the scene under `root` as a glb (or .gltf) at `file`: parts,
+## skeleton, skin and animations.
+static func write(root: Node, file: String) -> int:
+	var doc := GLTFDocument.new()
+	var st := GLTFState.new()
+	var err := doc.append_from_scene(root, st)
+	if err != OK:
+		return err
+	DirAccess.make_dir_recursive_absolute(file.get_base_dir())
+	return doc.write_to_filesystem(st, file)
+
+
+## A primitive as an editable mesh, about a metre across.
+static func primitive(kind: String) -> ArrayMesh:
+	var p: PrimitiveMesh
+	match kind:
+		"box":
+			p = BoxMesh.new()
+		"cylinder":
+			var c := CylinderMesh.new()
+			c.top_radius = 0.5; c.bottom_radius = 0.5; c.height = 1.0; c.radial_segments = 24; c.rings = 1
+			p = c
+		"cone":
+			var c := CylinderMesh.new()
+			c.top_radius = 0.0; c.bottom_radius = 0.5; c.height = 1.0; c.radial_segments = 24; c.rings = 1
+			p = c
+		"sphere":
+			var s := SphereMesh.new()
+			s.radius = 0.5; s.height = 1.0; s.radial_segments = 24; s.rings = 12
+			p = s
+		"plane":
+			var pl := PlaneMesh.new()
+			pl.size = Vector2(1, 1)
+			p = pl
+		"torus":
+			var t := TorusMesh.new()
+			t.inner_radius = 0.3; t.outer_radius = 0.5; t.rings = 24; t.ring_segments = 12
+			p = t
+		_:
+			return null
+	var a := p.get_mesh_arrays()
+	a[Mesh.ARRAY_TANGENT] = null
+	var m := ArrayMesh.new()
+	m.add_surface_from_arrays(Mesh.PRIMITIVE_TRIANGLES, a)
+	m.resource_name = kind.capitalize()
+	return m
+
+
+## A physically based material for a new part (and the presets' base).
+static func default_material() -> StandardMaterial3D:
+	var m := StandardMaterial3D.new()
+	m.resource_name = "Default"
+	m.albedo_color = Color(0.72, 0.72, 0.74)
+	m.metallic = 0.6
+	m.roughness = 0.4
+	return m
+
+
+## The materials offered besides a model's own: the game's looks
+## ([name, colour, metallic, roughness, emission colour, emission energy]).
+const PRESETS := [
+	["Bronze", Color(0.72, 0.45, 0.2), 1.0, 0.35, Color.BLACK, 0.0],
+	["Gold", Color(1.0, 0.78, 0.34), 1.0, 0.25, Color.BLACK, 0.0],
+	["Steel", Color(0.62, 0.64, 0.68), 1.0, 0.3, Color.BLACK, 0.0],
+	["Dark metal", Color(0.16, 0.17, 0.2), 0.9, 0.45, Color.BLACK, 0.0],
+	["Painted armour", Color(0.85, 0.82, 0.75), 0.3, 0.45, Color.BLACK, 0.0],
+	["Minoan red", Color(0.62, 0.12, 0.08), 0.2, 0.5, Color.BLACK, 0.0],
+	["Navy", Color(0.08, 0.12, 0.3), 0.3, 0.5, Color.BLACK, 0.0],
+	["Cloth", Color(0.8, 0.74, 0.62), 0.0, 0.9, Color.BLACK, 0.0],
+	["Stone", Color(0.7, 0.66, 0.6), 0.0, 0.85, Color.BLACK, 0.0],
+	["Glow (cyan)", Color(0.2, 0.8, 1.0), 0.0, 0.4, Color(0.3, 0.85, 1.0), 3.0],
+	["Glow (amber)", Color(1.0, 0.6, 0.2), 0.0, 0.4, Color(1.0, 0.6, 0.2), 3.0],
+]
+
+
+static func preset(i: int) -> StandardMaterial3D:
+	var p: Array = PRESETS[i]
+	var m := StandardMaterial3D.new()
+	m.resource_name = p[0]
+	m.albedo_color = p[1]
+	m.metallic = p[2]
+	m.roughness = p[3]
+	if p[5] > 0.0:
+		m.emission_enabled = true
+		m.emission = p[4]
+		m.emission_energy_multiplier = p[5]
+	return m

files.explanation: Duplicate, merge by distance and auto merge, inset, loop cut, select loop and ring - plain geometry functions on an EditMesh plus the hooks into the editor's transforms.

hunks.diff:
@@ -1,0 +1,1192 @@ 
+extends Node
+## More of the mesh editor's edit-mode tools (a node of the editor, `ed`):
+## - Duplicate (Shift+D): the selected faces copied (their points too) - the copy selected and moved.
+## - Merge by distance (Alt+M): the selected points (all, if none) closer than `merge_dist` made one;
+##   Auto merge: after each move / turn / scale, the points it moved onto others welded to them.
+## - Inset (I): a ring of new faces inside the selected region's border, its width by the mouse
+##   (or typed); click keeps, right-click / Esc cancels.
+## - Loop cut (Ctrl+R): the ring of quads across the edge under the mouse shown; a click cuts a new
+##   edge loop through it, then the mouse slides it along the ring; click keeps it (right-click /
+##   Esc: kept in the middle).
+## - Select loop / ring (Alt+click an edge; the buttons from the selected edges): the edge loop
+##   straight on through four-way points, or the edges across a ring of quads; in face mode the
+##   faces of the ring, in vertex mode the loop's points.
+## The geometry (static, on an EditMesh) is plain data; the rest drives the editor's transform
+## (xf: "step" / "on_cancel" / "name" - mesh_editor.gd calls them) and its undo (one step each).
+
+const EditMesh := preload("res://scripts/editor/mesh/edit_mesh.gd")
+const DEFAULT_DIST := 0.0001
+
+var ed: Control
+## Merge by distance's threshold (metres, the part's own space).
+var merge_dist := DEFAULT_DIST
+## Points a transform moved onto others welded to them when it ends.
+var auto_merge := false
+## The loop cut is waiting for a click (the ring under the mouse shown).
+var cutting := false
+var _ring := {}
+var _alt_at := Vector2(-1, -1)
+var _auto_btn: Button
+var _dist_spin: SpinBox
+
+
+func setup(editor: Control) -> void:
+	ed = editor
+	name = "MeshOps"
+
+
+# --- the geometry (an EditMesh) ----------------------------------------------------
+
+## Copies of the faces flagged in `tsel` (whole faces): their vertices copied (every attribute)
+## onto new points at the same places, the copies' faces new ids. Returns the new points.
+static func duplicate_faces(em, tsel: PackedByteArray) -> PackedInt32Array:
+	var n0: int = em.points.size()
+	var pts: PackedVector3Array = em.points
+	var np := PackedInt32Array()
+	np.resize(n0)
+	np.fill(-1)
+	var out := PackedInt32Array()
+	var st: Array = em._starts(tsel)
+	var next: int = em.face_n
+	var fmap := {}
+	for si in em.surfs.size():
+		var starts: PackedInt32Array = st[si]
+		if starts.is_empty():
+			continue
+		var s = em.surfs[si]
+		var idx: PackedInt32Array = s.idx
+		var face: PackedInt32Array = s.face
+		var vm := {}
+		for i0 in starts:
+			for k in 3:
+				var v: int = idx[i0 + k]
+				if not vm.has(v):
+					var p: int = s.vp[v]
+					if np[p] < 0:
+						np[p] = pts.size()
+						out.append(pts.size())
+						pts.append(pts[p])
+					vm[v] = s.copy_vertex(v, np[p])
+				idx.append(vm[v])
+			var f: int = face[i0 / 3] if i0 / 3 < face.size() else -1
+			if not fmap.has(f):
+				fmap[f] = next
+				next += 1
+			face.append(fmap[f])
+		s.idx = idx
+		s.face = face
+	em.points = pts
+	em.derive()
+	return out
+
+
+## Point -> the point it becomes (`to`, itself if it stays): the points of `query` within `dist`
+## of a point of `targets` (both empty: all points) joined, through each other too. A group's
+## point is its lowest (`fixed` flags a point that stays where it is - one in a group leads it).
+## Returns {"to": PackedInt32Array, "at": {point: where}, "removed": int}.
+static func close_points(points: PackedVector3Array, query: PackedInt32Array, targets: PackedInt32Array, dist: float, fixed := PackedByteArray()) -> Dictionary:
+	var n := points.size()
+	var to := PackedInt32Array()
+	to.resize(n)
+	for i in n:
+		to[i] = i
+	if dist <= 0.0 or n < 2:
+		return {"to": to, "at": {}, "removed": 0}
+	if query.is_empty():
+		query = PackedInt32Array(range(n))
+	if targets.is_empty():
+		targets = query
+	var inv := 1.0 / dist
+	var grid := {}
+	for p in targets:
+		var c := Vector3i((points[p] * inv).floor())
+		if grid.has(c):
+			(grid[c] as Array).append(p)
+		else:
+			grid[c] = [p]
+	var d2 := dist * dist
+	var parent := to.duplicate()
+	var touched := {}
+	var lead := func(a: int, b: int) -> bool:   # (a leads b: fixed first, else the lower)
+		var fa := not fixed.is_empty() and fixed[a] == 1
+		var fb := not fixed.is_empty() and fixed[b] == 1
+		return fa and not fb or (fa == fb and a < b)
+	for q in query:
+		var c := Vector3i((points[q] * inv).floor())
+		for x in range(-1, 2):
+			for y in range(-1, 2):
+				for z in range(-1, 2):
+					var cell = grid.get(c + Vector3i(x, y, z))
+					if cell == null:
+						continue
+					for p: int in cell:
+						if p == q or points[p].distance_squared_to(points[q]) > d2:
+							continue
+						var ra := _find(parent, q)
+						var rb := _find(parent, p)
+						if ra == rb:
+							continue
+						if lead.call(ra, rb):
+							parent[rb] = ra
+						else:
+							parent[ra] = rb
+						touched[p] = true
+						touched[q] = true
+	var removed := 0
+	var sum := {}
+	var cnt := {}
+	for p in touched:
+		var r := _find(parent, p)
+		to[p] = r
+		if r != p:
+			removed += 1
+		sum[r] = sum.get(r, Vector3.ZERO) + points[p]
+		cnt[r] = cnt.get(r, 0) + 1
+	var at := {}
+	for r in sum:
+		at[r] = points[r] if not fixed.is_empty() and fixed[r] == 1 else sum[r] / float(cnt[r])
+	return {"to": to, "at": at, "removed": removed}
+
+
+static func _find(parent: PackedInt32Array, p: int) -> int:
+	var r := p
+	while parent[r] != r:
+		r = parent[r]
+	while parent[p] != r:
+		var nx := parent[p]
+		parent[p] = r
+		p = nx
+	return r
+
+
+## The points welded as `close` (close_points) says: each made the point it goes to (moved to
+## its place), triangles left with two corners on one point dropped, the points nothing uses
+## dropped. Returns old point -> new (-1: gone).
+static func weld(em, close: Dictionary) -> PackedInt32Array:
+	var to: PackedInt32Array = close["to"]
+	var at: Dictionary = close["at"]
+	var pts: PackedVector3Array = em.points
+	for r in at:
+		pts[r] = at[r]
+	em.points = pts
+	var touched := {}   # points merged into (a face on them may now double another)
+	for p in to.size():
+		if to[p] != p:
+			touched[to[p]] = true
+	var seen := {}      # a triangle's points (sorted) -> kept already
+	for s in em.surfs:
+		var vp: PackedInt32Array = s.vp
+		for v in vp.size():
+			vp[v] = to[vp[v]]
+		s.vp = vp
+		s.sync(pts, PackedInt32Array())
+		s.drop_degenerate()
+		# (faces welded onto each other - a copy merged back - kept once)
+		var kill := {}
+		for i in range(0, s.idx.size() - 2, 3):
+			var t := [s.vp[s.idx[i]], s.vp[s.idx[i + 1]], s.vp[s.idx[i + 2]]]
+			if not (touched.has(t[0]) or touched.has(t[1]) or touched.has(t[2])):
+				continue
+			t.sort()
+			var key := Vector3i(t[0], t[1], t[2])
+			if seen.has(key):
+				kill[i] = true
+			else:
+				seen[key] = true
+		if not kill.is_empty():
+			s.drop_tris(kill)
+		s.compact()
+	var map := _compact_map(em)
+	em.compact()
+	em.unused = false
+	em.derive()
+	var out := PackedInt32Array()   # (a point merged: the number of the one it went into)
+	out.resize(map.size())
+	for p in map.size():
+		out[p] = map[to[p]]
+	return out
+
+
+## What EditMesh.compact() will renumber the points to (old -> new, -1: dropped) - the
+## surfaces' unused vertices dropped first (as it does).
+static func _compact_map(em) -> PackedInt32Array:
+	var n: int = em.points.size()
+	var used := PackedByteArray()
+	used.resize(n)
+	for s in em.surfs:
+		s.compact()
+		for p in s.vp:
+			used[p] = 1
+	var map := PackedInt32Array()
+	map.resize(n)
+	var k := 0
+	for p in n:
+		if used[p]:
+			map[p] = k
+			k += 1
+		else:
+			map[p] = -1
+	return map
+
+
+## Inset: the faces flagged in `tsel` (a region) moved onto copies of their points, a ring of
+## quads along the region's border joining them to it (as an extrude whose top isn't lifted).
+## Returns {"ids": the border points' copies, "orig": their places, "dirs": the way each goes in
+## (along the faces, as far as the inset is wide - a corner further, its sides keeping the width),
+## "inner": all the region's points (new numbers), "ring": the border's points} - or {} if none.
+static func inset_region(em, tsel: PackedByteArray) -> Dictionary:
+	var n0: int = em.points.size()
+	var pts: PackedVector3Array = em.points
+	var np := PackedInt32Array()
+	np.resize(n0)
+	np.fill(-1)
+	var border := {}
+	var side := {}   # edge key -> [a, b, c]: a -> b along the region's triangle, c its third corner
+	for t in mini(tsel.size(), em.tri_count()):
+		if not tsel[t]:
+			continue
+		for k in 3:
+			var a: int = em.tris[t * 3 + k]
+			var b: int = em.tris[t * 3 + (k + 1) % 3]
+			var key := mini(a, b) * n0 + maxi(a, b)
+			border[key] = border.get(key, 0) + 1
+			side[key] = [a, b, em.tris[t * 3 + (k + 2) % 3]]
+			if np[a] < 0:
+				np[a] = pts.size()
+				pts.append(pts[a])
+	if border.is_empty():
+		return {}
+	# the way in at each border point: the sides' inward directions met
+	var ins := {}   # point -> [inward unit vectors]
+	for key in border:
+		if border[key] != 1:
+			continue
+		var s: Array = side[key]
+		var pa: Vector3 = pts[s[0]]
+		var pb: Vector3 = pts[s[1]]
+		var pc: Vector3 = pts[s[2]]
+		var e := (pb - pa).normalized()
+		var w := pc - pa
+		var u := (w - e * w.dot(e)).normalized()
+		for p in [s[0], s[1]]:
+			if ins.has(p):
+				(ins[p] as Array).append(u)
+			else:
+				ins[p] = [u]
+	if ins.is_empty():
+		return {}   # (a closed region - nothing to inset from)
+	em.points = pts
+	var st: Array = em._starts(tsel)
+	var next: int = em.face_n
+	for si in em.surfs.size():
+		if not (st[si] as PackedInt32Array).is_empty():
+			next = em.surfs[si].extrude(st[si], np, border, n0, next)
+			em.surfs[si].recalc_normals()
+	var map := _compact_map(em)   # (the region's inside points: only the copies use them now)
+	em.compact()
+	em.derive()
+	var ids := PackedInt32Array()
+	var orig := PackedVector3Array()
+	var dirs := PackedVector3Array()
+	var ring := PackedInt32Array()
+	for p in ins:
+		var us: Array = ins[p]
+		var m := Vector3.ZERO
+		for u: Vector3 in us:
+			m += u
+		var d: Vector3 = us[0]
+		if m.length() > 1e-6:
+			var mn := m.normalized()
+			var c := 1.0
+			for u: Vector3 in us:
+				c = minf(c, mn.dot(u))
+			d = mn / maxf(c, 0.25)
+		ids.append(map[np[p]])
+		orig.append(em.points[map[np[p]]])
+		dirs.append(d)
+		if map[p] >= 0:
+			ring.append(map[p])
+	var inner := PackedInt32Array()
+	for p in n0:
+		if np[p] >= 0 and map[np[p]] >= 0:
+			inner.append(map[np[p]])
+	return {"ids": ids, "orig": orig, "dirs": dirs, "inner": inner, "ring": ring}
+
+
+## The faces (n-gons) along edge `e` (a triangle of each).
+static func _faces_on(em, e: int) -> Array:
+	var out := {}
+	for t in em.edge_tri_list(e):
+		if not out.has(em.tri_face[t]):
+			out[em.tri_face[t]] = t
+	return out.values()
+
+
+## From edge a -> b into the face of triangle `t`: on across quads to their opposite sides.
+## [[a, b] of each side crossed, in order], [a triangle of each quad crossed], closed (back at `e0`).
+static func _walk(em, a: int, b: int, t: int, e0: int, seen: Dictionary) -> Array:
+	var sides := []
+	var quads := PackedInt32Array()
+	var closed := false
+	while true:
+		var f: int = em.tri_face[t]
+		if seen.has(f):
+			break
+		var lp: PackedInt32Array = em.poly_loop(t)
+		if lp.size() != 4:
+			break
+		var i := lp.find(a)
+		if i < 0:
+			break
+		var na := -1
+		var nb := -1
+		if lp[(i + 1) % 4] == b:
+			na = lp[(i + 3) % 4]
+			nb = lp[(i + 2) % 4]
+		elif lp[(i + 3) % 4] == b:
+			na = lp[(i + 1) % 4]
+			nb = lp[(i + 2) % 4]
+		else:
+			break
+		var ne: int = em.edge(na, nb)
+		if ne < 0:
+			break
+		seen[f] = true
+		quads.append(t)
+		if ne == e0:
+			closed = true
+			break
+		sides.append([na, nb])
+		var nt := -1
+		var lst: PackedInt32Array = em.edge_tri_list(ne)
+		if lst.size() != 2 and _faces_on(em, ne).size() != 2:
+			break
+		for u in lst:
+			if em.tri_face[u] != f:
+				nt = u
+				break
+		if nt < 0:
+			break
+		a = na
+		b = nb
+		t = nt
+	return [sides, quads, closed]
+
+
+## The ring of quads across edge a -> b: {"sides": [[a, b]...] - the edges it crosses, each a
+## the same side as the first's a; "quads": a triangle of each quad between side k and k + 1
+## (closed: and the last back to the first); "closed"}. Stops at a face not a quad, an open
+## edge or a quad already crossed.
+static func ring(em, a: int, b: int) -> Dictionary:
+	var e0: int = em.edge(a, b)
+	if e0 < 0:
+		return {"sides": [], "quads": PackedInt32Array(), "closed": false}
+	var faces := _faces_on(em, e0)
+	var seen := {}
+	var fwd: Array = _walk(em, a, b, faces[0], e0, seen) if faces.size() > 0 else [[], PackedInt32Array(), false]
+	if fwd[2]:
+		return {"sides": [[a, b]] + fwd[0], "quads": fwd[1], "closed": true}
+	var back: Array = _walk(em, a, b, faces[1], e0, seen) if faces.size() == 2 else [[], PackedInt32Array(), false]
+	var sides: Array = (back[0] as Array).duplicate()
+	sides.reverse()
+	var quads: PackedInt32Array = back[1]
+	quads.reverse()
+	sides.append([a, b])
+	sides.append_array(fwd[0])
+	quads.append_array(fwd[1])
+	return {"sides": sides, "quads": quads, "closed": false}
+
+
+## The knife chain (EditMesh.knife_apply) of a loop cut through ring `r`, `f` of the way from
+## each side's a to its b.
+static func ring_chain(em, r: Dictionary, f := 0.5) -> Dictionary:
+	var nodes := []
+	for s in r["sides"]:
+		var e: int = em.edge(s[0], s[1])
+		nodes.append(em.node_on_edge(e, f if em.edges[e * 2] == s[0] else 1.0 - f))
+	if r["closed"] and not nodes.is_empty():
+		nodes.append(nodes[0])
+	return {"nodes": nodes, "segs": PackedInt32Array(r["quads"])}
+
+
+## A shown edge (between faces, not a face's diagonal).
+static func _shown(em, e: int) -> bool:
+	return e >= 0 and not em.edge_inner[e]
+
+
+## The edge after `e` at its point `p` going straight on: the one of the four there that
+## shares no face with it (an open edge: the next open one); -1 at a pole or an end.
+static func _next_in_loop(em, e: int, p: int) -> int:
+	var fe := {}
+	for t in em.edge_tri_list(e):
+		fe[em.tri_face[t]] = true
+	var shown := []
+	for k in range(em.adj_start[p], em.adj_start[p + 1]):
+		var e2: int = em.edge(p, em.adj[k])
+		if e2 != e and _shown(em, e2):
+			shown.append(e2)
+	if fe.size() == 1:   # (an open edge: along the border)
+		var open := []
+		for e2 in shown:
+			if _faces_on(em, e2).size() == 1:
+				open.append(e2)
+		return open[0] if open.size() == 1 else -1
+	if shown.size() != 3:
+		return -1
+	var out := -1
+	for e2 in shown:
+		var shares := false
+		for t in em.edge_tri_list(e2):
+			if fe.has(em.tri_face[t]):
+				shares = true
+		if not shares:
+			if out >= 0:
+				return -1
+			out = e2
+	return out
+
+
+## Edge `e0`'s loop: on from both its ends while the way goes straight on (edges, it first).
+static func edge_loop(em, e0: int) -> PackedInt32Array:
+	var out := PackedInt32Array([e0])
+	var seen := {e0: true}
+	for end in 2:
+		var e := e0
+		var p: int = em.edges[e0 * 2 + end]
+		while true:
+			var nx := _next_in_loop(em, e, p)
+			if nx < 0 or seen.has(nx):
+				break
+			seen[nx] = true
+			out.append(nx)
+			p = em.edges[nx * 2] if em.edges[nx * 2 + 1] == p else em.edges[nx * 2 + 1]
+			e = nx
+		if end == 0 and out.size() > 1 and _next_in_loop(em, e, p) == e0:
+			break   # (round: closed)
+	return out
+
+
+## Edge `e`'s ring: the edges across the quads either side of it, it too.
+static func edge_ring(em, e: int) -> PackedInt32Array:
+	var r := ring(em, em.edges[e * 2], em.edges[e * 2 + 1])
+	var out := PackedInt32Array()
+	for s in r["sides"]:
+		out.append(em.edge(s[0], s[1]))
+	return out
+

+## The new tools' buttons (the EDIT MESH panel): a row of icons, and Merge by distance's
+## threshold with Auto merge.
+func build_panel(box: Control) -> void:
+	var row := HFlowContainer.new()
+	row.name = "MeshOpsRow"
+	row.add_theme_constant_override("h_separation", 2)
+	row.add_theme_constant_override("v_separation", 2)
+	for it in items():
+		row.add_child(_icon_btn(it[0], it[1], it[2], it[3], it[4]))
+	_auto_btn = _icon_btn("m_auto_merge", "Auto merge", "", "After each move, turn or scale, the points it put within the merge distance of another\npoint are welded to it (the other stays where it is). One undo step with the move.", func(): set_auto_merge(not auto_merge))
+	_auto_btn.toggle_mode = true
+	_auto_btn.button_pressed = auto_merge
+	row.add_child(_auto_btn)
+	_dist_spin = SpinBox.new()
+	_dist_spin.name = "MergeDistance"
+	_dist_spin.min_value = 0.000001
+	_dist_spin.max_value = 10.0
+	_dist_spin.step = 0.000001
+	_dist_spin.value = merge_dist
+	_dist_spin.custom_minimum_size.x = 86
+	_dist_spin.tooltip_text = EditorIcons.tip("Merge by distance: distance", "", "Points closer than this (metres, in the part's own space) are made one by Merge by distance\nand by Auto merge.")
+	_dist_spin.value_changed.connect(func(v): merge_dist = v)
+	row.add_child(_dist_spin)
+	box.add_child(row)
+
+
+func _icon_btn(icon: String, title: String, keys: String, help: String, cb: Callable) -> Button:
+	var b := Button.new()
+	b.name = "Op_" + title.validate_node_name()
+	b.focus_mode = Control.FOCUS_NONE
+	b.icon = EditorIcons.get_icon(icon)
+	b.icon_alignment = HORIZONTAL_ALIGNMENT_CENTER
+	b.custom_minimum_size = Vector2(32, 30)
+	b.tooltip_text = EditorIcons.tip(title, keys, help)
+	IconAnim.attach(b, icon)
+	b.pressed.connect(func():
+		if ed.em == null:
+			ed.enter_edit(true)
+		if ed.em != null:
+			cb.call())
+	return b
+
+
+## [icon, title, keys, help, action] of each tool (the panel row and the right-click menu).
+func items() -> Array:
+	return [
+		["m_duplicate_mesh", "Duplicate selection", "Shift+D", "The selected faces copied, their points too, then moved with the mouse (click keeps it where it is;\nthe copy stays even if the move is cancelled). Points and edges alone copy nothing: the mesh is faces.", duplicate_selection],
+		["m_inset", "Inset", "I", "A ring of new faces inside the selected faces' border (the selection inset as one region):\nthe mouse towards the middle makes it wider, or type the width (metres); click keeps it,\nright-click / Esc cancels.", begin_inset],
+		["m_loop_cut", "Loop cut", "Ctrl+R", "A new edge loop round a ring of quads: point at an edge to see the ring across it, click to cut,\nthen slide it along with the mouse and click to keep it (right-click / Esc: kept in the middle).", begin_loopcut],
+		["m_sel_loop", "Select loop", "Alt+click", "The selected edges' loops: on straight through each four-way point to a pole or an open end\n(Alt+click an edge: its loop; Shift+Alt+click adds; in face mode the ring of quads, in vertex mode its points).", select_loops],
+		["m_sel_ring", "Select ring", "", "The edges across the ring of quads either side of each selected edge.", select_rings],
+		["m_merge_dist", "Merge by distance", "Alt+M", "The selected points (all, if none are) closer to each other than the distance beside it\nmade one - each group at its middle. Says how many went.", func(): merge_by_distance()],
+	]
+

+## The right-click menu's group of them (in edit mode).
+func menu_items() -> Array:
+	var out := []
+	for it in items():
+		out.append([it[0], it[1], it[2], it[3].split("\n")[0], it[4], true])
+	out.append(["m_auto_merge", "Auto merge " + ("off" if auto_merge else "on"), "", "Points moved onto others are welded to them when the move ends.", func(): set_auto_merge(not auto_merge), true])
